item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.7
item.description:
**⌃⌥G leaves full-screen windows where they are, and the desktop is no longer taken for a window.** ⌃⌥G no longer switches to a full-screen app, or to another Desktop, to bring back one window of a group: it brings back the windows that are here and leaves those where they are. A group that is all on another Desktop still comes back there. On the Finder desktop, the snap keys beep instead of opening Snap Assist beside nothing.
Also fixed: a window fitted beside a wide one (such as Proton Mail) takes its room back once the wide one goes; snapping beside Proton Mail no longer waits for its app; a third ⌃⌥H while windows are still going into the Dock; ⌃⌥Z after a layout applied while a window was moving; and a small memory leak. Settings now tells you when another app holds one of your shortcuts for itself.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.6
item.description:
**Snapping starts sooner, and snap groups work with apps that will not shrink.** SnapWindows asks a window's app fewer questions before moving it, so a snap starts sooner, most of all while a browser plays a video. Groups with a window that keeps a size of its own (an app's minimum width, such as Proton Mail's) now stay a group: ⌃⌥H, minimizing together and Fill the gap work with them.
Also fixed: ⌃⌥Z after bringing windows back from the Dock, Fill the gap after you move a window yourself, a double click in Snap Assist, and closing the Permissions window opened from Settings. ⌘W and Esc now close Settings. With several displays, a display that came back long ago no longer moves its windows when another display arrives.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.5
item.description:
**⌃⌥G always opens the list of snap groups.** If the window you are in belongs to a group, that group is already highlighted: press Return (or click it) to bring it back, or Delete (⌫) to ungroup it. Nothing moves until you choose, and you no longer press ⌃⌥G twice.
Grouping works as before: snap a window to one side, pick another window in Snap Assist, and the two become a group. Until you have one (none are kept after a restart), the list says how to make one.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.4
item.description:
**Ungroup from the ⌃⌥G list.** The list of snap groups (⌃⌥G) now has an **Ungroup** button for each group. With the keyboard, highlight a group with ↑ ↓ and press Delete (⌫). You no longer need the menu bar icon to ungroup.
In a window that is in a group, ⌃⌥G brings that group back; press ⌃⌥G again to open the list with that group highlighted.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.3
item.description:
**Snap Assist no longer flickers, or hides the window beside it.** The window you pick now comes forward only once it is in its place, so a full-screen window no longer covers the screen for a moment and then jumps. And only that window comes forward: picking one of Safari's two windows no longer brings the other one along over the window you snapped first.
**Ungroup.** To stop two windows acting as a group, open the SnapWindows menu > Snap groups and choose **Ungroup** for that group.
**⌃⌥C from a half.** A window in a half or a third now goes to the middle of the screen at the size it had before you snapped it, instead of staying a tall strip down the middle.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.2
item.description:
**Smooth with every app, not only browsers.** When SnapWindows moves a window that changes size, the window now takes its new size at once and then slides into place, as Claude and Safari have since 1.13.1. Apps that are slow to lay themselves out, such as Messages, no longer stutter or lag on the way.
To change it: **Settings > General > Resize windows** (in one step for every app, for browsers and web apps only, or gradually). To have one app resize gradually, set it to **Resize gradually** in Settings > Apps.

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.1
item.description:
**Smoother with browsers and web apps.** Safari, Chrome, Firefox and apps built on Chrome's engine (Claude, ChatGPT, Slack, Notion, VS Code, Spotify) now take their new size at once and then slide into place, instead of being resized through every size on the way. A window playing a video no longer stutters while you put another window beside it.
You can switch this off in **Settings > General** ("Resize browsers and web apps in one step"), or keep one app's full glide with **Glide as usual** in Settings > Apps (which also treats it as usual, like an app not on the list).

item.title: SnapWindows 1.13.0
item.description:
**SnapWindows now updates itself.** Once a day it checks for a new version and offers it, with what is new; it installs only when you choose **Install Update** and then **Install and Relaunch**, and restarts by itself a few seconds later.
- **Check for Updates…** is in the menu and in Settings, which also shows which version you have. - A new version does not interrupt you: the menu bar icon gets a small dot, and the menu says **Update to SnapWindows …**. - Every version is signed, and SnapWindows installs nothing that is not.
